@ShashankRaina  It does, imagine this at a very large scale. AC was gone because that year whirlpool launched alloy AC instead of traditionally used copper, that alloy got holes in it just after the warranty is expired, repair guy said it would cost 10000 to repair it, AC cost itself was 30000, plus there is no guarantee that the problem wont repeat. Who took the decision to switch to alloy and across how many of their product categories? It destroys the brand value and trust and it only multiplies unless there are measures to rectify it. This must have happened to almost all of their ACs, those customers will never buy whirlpool again. I dont know how naive you are, this anchor recommending whirlpool and trying to trap retailers is the proof of that share price hampering, otherwise why would they recommend.

@Deepakk12345 firstly, your sample size is very small. Almost impossible to judge a company based on personal experience and assumptions.

If share price determines quality of materials, then HUL and HDFC bank should be giving bad products/services. ITC would not be giving good products. TCS and infosys software and services would decline. Zomato and lenskart customer service must be top class with almost 0 bad reviews and products.

I agree that a bad product lineup or faulty products would impact future earnings. But they also sell multiple products. The share price generally follows earnings in the long term but in the short term, it can be influenced by many other factors and become overvalued.

Lastly, the anchor has actually highlighted risks also along with pros and asked "would you invest" It isn't a recommendation, just an open ended question. Only requires you to listen carefully and not be paranoid that everyone is out to loot you. It's only for information.
